mem.t: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

lessons.title: God's Kindness Leads to Repentance
lessons.theme: It isn't scolding that brings us back; it is kindness that leads us home

v: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, forbearance, and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,

lessons.still: Quietly reflect: did you turn back to God because you were scolded, or because you were treated with kindness? Let a picture of God's kindness to you come to mind. Stay there, and say to the Lord, “It was your kindness that led me home.”
teach: The North Wind and the Sun made a bet over which of them could make a traveller take off his coat. The harder the North Wind blew, the more tightly the traveller wrapped his coat around himself; but when the Sun shone warmly, he took the coat off of his own accord. The fable expresses a spiritual principle: harshness makes people defensive, while warmth makes them open up.

Paul says God's kindness “leads you to repentance.” The word “leads” is like a shepherd leading his sheep, gentle yet firm. Titus says God saved us not because of righteous things we had done, but according to his mercy, when “the kindness of God our Savior” appeared. Repentance doesn't come from being scolded awake; it comes from being melted by love.

The original word for kindness carries the sense of being useful, fitting and gentle toward others; it is goodness with warmth, actively given. When we want to change other people, we often use the North Wind's method: criticism, blame and pressure. The mindset shift: God changed me through kindness, so I too will treat my 2 with kindness and let God's warmth melt hearts.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-ruled person tries to change others by force, provoking pride so that both sides lose; the self-emptied person opens hearts with kindness, and humility inspires humility. The fruit of kindness is not self-cultivation; it is God's kindness in Christ shining naturally out of a self-emptied person.
q: Who is God? — God leads you to repentance with kindness rather than scolding. What kind of God does this show you?
Who am I? — When you want to change someone, do you more often act like the North Wind or the Sun?
How shall I respond? — What act of kindness will you put in place of a criticism today?
lessons.jesus: Zacchaeus climbed a tree to watch the spectacle, perhaps also braced for people's pointing fingers. But Jesus stopped and called him by name: “Today I must stay at your house.” Not a word of rebuke, yet Zacchaeus repented on the spot. Jesus' kindness was more powerful than any condemnation.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for leading me to repentance with kindness, and for saving me not by my righteousness but by your mercy. I confess that I often try to change others with criticism and pressure. Make me like you, melting hearts with the warmth of kindness, so that people taste your grace through me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down a time when God's kindness turned you back
Today, replace one criticism you want to make with an act of kindness
For one of my 2s: show your goodwill toward them in some small way
lessons.noon: “Not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?” — Lord, right now let me be warm toward people, like the sun.

lessons.title: David's Kindness to Mephibosheth
lessons.theme: Kindness actively seeks out those who cannot repay

v: David said, “Is there yet any who is left of Saul’s house, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?”

David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually.”

lessons.still: Imagine yourself as Mephibosheth: lame in both feet, living in remote Lo Debar, summoned before the king and bowing down in fear. Then hear the king say, “Don't be afraid.” Quietly let these words become the Lord's words to you.
teach: In the ancient world, a new king would often wipe out the descendants of the previous royal house to prevent future trouble. David did the opposite. He took the initiative to ask, “Is there anyone left of the house of Saul?” not to destroy them but to show them kindness. The question itself is where kindness begins: kindness does not wait to be asked; it goes looking.

Mephibosheth was lame in both feet and a descendant of David's old enemy; he was of no use to David and might even be a threat. Yet because of the covenant he had made with Jonathan, David showed him kindness: he restored his lands and let him eat at the king's table continually. Mephibosheth's response was, “What is your servant, that you should look at such a dead dog as I am?” Kindness shines most brightly when it reaches the undeserving.

Each of us is a spiritual Mephibosheth: crippled by sin, yet invited to the King's banquet because of the covenant God made in Christ. The mindset shift: I show kindness to people not because they deserve it, but because I was shown kindness first. Today, is there someone around you, someone “left of the house of Saul”, waiting to be shown kindness?
lessons.light: 321 Light: David laid down a king's power. He did not use it for revenge but for kindness, and this is the authority of the self-emptied life. Those who let Jesus reign will use everything in their hands to bless others. Kindness is the overflow of Christ's life, not the product of self-cultivation.
q: Who is God? — Like David, God takes the initiative to seek you out and invite you to his table. How does that make you feel?
Who am I? — Are you kind only to those who are useful to you and can repay you?
How shall I respond? — Who around you is someone “left of the house of Saul”, needing you to go and show them kindness?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don't call your friends… But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind; and you will be blessed” (Luke 14:12–14). He himself did exactly that, eating with tax collectors and sinners.
lessons.pray: Lord, I am that lame Mephibosheth, yet for Christ's sake you have invited me to your table. Thank you for seeking me out. Help me too to seek out those who cannot repay me, and to use all that you have given me to show them kindness, for your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Read 2 Samuel 9, noticing each of David's acts of kindness
Invite someone who is often overlooked for a cup of tea or a meal
For one of my 2s: take the initiative to do something for them that they cannot repay
lessons.noon: “You will eat bread at my table continually.” — Lord, right now I sit at the banquet of your grace.

lessons.title: Clothed with Kindness
lessons.theme: Kindness is not a single act but a heart we put on

v: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
“Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.

lessons.still: As you get dressed this morning, notice yourself putting on each item of clothing. Then, in your heart, “put on” these one by one as well: compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience. Say to the Lord, “Lord, today I go out wearing your heart.”
teach: We get dressed every morning; nobody skips it because they wore clothes yesterday. Paul says we are to have “a heart of compassion, kindness…”, and the word he uses means to “put on”. Kindness is not an occasional good deed; it is clothing we put on every morning, so that when people see us they see the likeness of Christ.

Paul first states who we are, “God's chosen ones, holy and beloved,” and only then says what to put on. We don't put on kindness in order to be loved; we put on kindness because we are already loved. Jesus also said: be merciful, just as your Father is merciful. Kindness is the family likeness; children resemble their Father.

Paul specifically mentions “if anyone has a complaint against another.” Kindness is tested most in relationships where there is friction. The mindset shift: kindness doesn't depend on my mood or on who the other person is; it depends on who I am. I am beloved, so I choose to put on a kind heart every day, even toward someone I have friction with.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Putting on the new self means taking off the old, self-ruled self. The five qualities Paul lists here (compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience) are the very pattern of the self-emptied life. The focus is on Jesus, not on whether the other person deserves it. Kindness is the natural overflow of Christ's life in a self-emptied person.
q: Who is God? — “Holy and beloved”: this is what God calls you. Do you believe it?
Who am I? — Does your kindness depend on your mood or on who the other person is?
How shall I respond? — How will you remind yourself to “put on” a kind heart today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus saw a widow at the funeral of her only son, he “had compassion on her, and said to her, ‘Don't cry,’” and then raised her son to life. No one asked him; he stopped of his own accord. Kindness was not an occasional act for him; it was the heart he always wore.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for calling me holy and beloved. Today I will put on a heart of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience. Make me merciful as you are merciful, so that even with those I have friction with I can bear with them and forgive them, just as you forgave me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: As you get dressed this morning, pray silently, “I put on kindness”
Show a small kindness to someone you have friction with
For one of my 2s: today, answer everything they say in a gentle tone
lessons.noon: “Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.” — Lord, right now I put on your kindness.

lessons.title: Kindness in Our Words
lessons.theme: A word that builds others up is the most common fruit of kindness

v: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

lessons.still: Think back over what you said yesterday. Which words did someone good? Which might have hurt someone? Don't beat yourself up; just bring it honestly before the Lord. Then ask him to guard your mouth today so that your words carry kindness.
teach: It's easy to squeeze toothpaste out of the tube, but almost impossible to put it back. Words are the same: once spoken, they cannot be taken back. We may not do many great things in a day, but we say thousands of words. Our speech is the most everyday place for the fruit of kindness, and also the place where it is most easily seen, or where we most easily wound.

Paul says to speak “only what is good for building others up.” “Building up” is originally a construction word. Every word is a brick: it can build a wall, or it can tear a house down. Proverbs says, “A gentle answer turns away wrath.” Say the same thing gently and anger subsides; say it harshly and anger flares up.

Kindness in our words does not mean saying only nice things and never the truth; it means speaking the truth in love, choosing a time and a way that builds others up. The mindset shift: before speaking, ask three questions. Is it true? Is it necessary? Will it build up? Let the Holy Spirit be Lord before we open our mouths.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Out of the heart flow the springs of life, and our words also pour out from the heart. The self-ruled person speaks to prove themselves and win; the self-emptied person speaks to build others up and glorify God. Speaking from the heart by the Spirit means letting Jesus reign over our tongues.
q: Who is God? — God created all things by his word. What power does his word have for you?
Who am I? — In what situations do you most often speak harshly?
How shall I respond? — To whom will you speak a word that builds them up today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus preached in the synagogue at Nazareth, “all testified about him, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth” (Luke 4:22). To the woman caught in adultery he said, “Neither do I condemn you”; to Peter he said, “Feed my sheep.” Every word he spoke was full of grace and truth.
lessons.pray: Lord, guard my mouth so that today I speak no corrupt words, only words that build others up. When I want to hit back, help me give a gentle answer that turns away wrath. Let your gracious words flow from my mouth, giving grace to those who hear. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before you speak, ask: Is it true? Is it necessary? Will it build up?
Today, take the initiative to praise a specific strength in someone
For one of my 2s: send them a message of encouragement
lessons.noon: “A gentle answer turns away wrath.” — Lord, right now guard my mouth.

lessons.title: Showing Kindness to My 2
lessons.theme: Be kind to one another, just as God in Christ forgave me

v: Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice.
And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

lessons.still: Open your “My 2 List” and ask the Holy Spirit to show you whom you are to show kindness to this week. If you still hold bitterness or resentment toward them, first hand it honestly to the Lord. Then think of how the Lord has been kind to you, and carry that kindness to that person.
teach: Before a gardener plants flowers, he must clear away the stones and weeds; otherwise even the best seed will not grow. Paul likewise speaks of putting off before putting on: first put away bitterness, wrath, anger, shouting, slander and malice, and then “be kind to one another.” The fruit of kindness cannot grow in a field of bitterness.

Ephesians 4:32 contains three actions: be kind to one another, be tender-hearted, forgive one another. The power for all of them lies in the final phrase: “just as God in Christ forgave you.” We don't show kindness on the strength of the other person's behaviour, but on the strength of the forgiveness of the cross. Those who have been forgiven much love much, and are kind in abundance.

This week we have seen God's kindness leading to repentance, David's kindness reaching out, putting on a kind heart, and kindness in our words. Now show kindness concretely to one of your 2s. Kindness is the warmth of goodness, and goodness is kindness in action; next week we will learn the next fruit, closely tied to kindness: goodness.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Building God's kingdom system begins with one act of forgiveness. Bitterness is the root of the self-ruled life: I want justice, I want to be the judge. Forgiveness is the fruit of the self-emptied life: handing judgement to God and returning to our place. Kindness is not self-cultivation; it is Christ's forgiveness flowing through us.
q: Who is God? — How much has God forgiven you in Christ? As you think about this, how do you respond?
Who am I? — Is there still bitterness in your heart blocking the growth of the fruit of kindness?
How shall I respond? — This week, toward which 2 will you show kindness, and with what concrete action?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus not only forgave those who crucified him; he also said to the repentant thief beside him, “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” In his moment of deepest pain, he was still kind, giving the hope of heaven to someone who did not deserve it.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, thank you that in Christ all my sins have been forgiven. I hand you the bitterness, resentment and anger in my heart; please take them away. This week I will be kind to one of my 2s, tender-hearted and forgiving, just as you forgave me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For one of my 2s: do one concrete act of kindness this week
Write down one bitterness you need to let go of, and lay it at the foot of the cross
lessons.noon: “Just as God also in Christ forgave you.” — Lord, right now let your forgiveness flow through me to them.
